title: Synthetic network-societies batch 2 statements
description: Pilot groups copied verbatim, plus campaign-local statements for the abortion forum, gender conduct, and voting. Accepted bridge wording is not copied here.
notes: Synthetic campaign only. Do not copy these into seed-content/.

Groups crypto-merchants, civic-assimilation, christian-teaching, home-learning, and shared-goods are copied from network-societies-v1-pilot-statements.json so this collection can load on its own. Edit those texts in the pilot file and re-copy; do not rewrite them here.

groups.title: Crypto-friendly merchant trials in Owen Sound

statements.text: I want a business in Grey County, Ontario, to be able to take a blockchain payment from a customer who asks to pay that way.
I want shops in Grey County to refuse customer payments in crypto.
I want a willing shop and a willing customer in Grey County to be able to complete a payment when a bank has blocked that customer.

groups.title: Shared civic life in Grey County
notes: The board is the assimilation want, two constituencies that already say it, a milder English sentence that does not, and a refusal. Adam called this good enough on 2026-10-20. A 2026-10-21 deepseek-v3.2 pass blessed some-immigration and fewer-newcomers toward assimilate, and refused the English sentence, the refusal, and the reverse arrows. Those two blesses are allowed as live-attester-recorded-bless. They are not bridge roles. Sessions and the park season are projects aligned to assimilate.

statements.text: If people from other cultures and other languages live in Grey County, Ontario, I want them to assimilate.
I want Grey County to keep welcoming some people from other cultures and other languages, and I want those people to assimilate.
I would rather fewer people from other cultures and other languages moved to Grey County. If people like that live here, I want them to assimilate.
I don't have a strong view on how many newcomers Grey County should take. People around here speak English, and I want people who live here to get along in English.
I want people in Grey County who come from other cultures and languages to be able to keep those cultures and languages, and I do not want them expected to assimilate.

groups.title: Christian teaching resources in Grey County
notes: Rewritten 2026-10-20. Adam called this good enough for now. Two wants, plus a refusal of sharing notes and a refusal to mix civic transcription with church teaching. Naming a confession and refusing a joint doctrinal statement are inside the notes want. Stating qualifications and doctrine is inside the independent-church want. The old midweek, rota, confession, and joint-doctrine ids are deleted.

statements.text: I want more freely available teaching notes that people from many English-speaking churches can use. I want those notes to name the confession and the other assumptions they rely on, and I do not want the churches that use them to have to publish a joint statement of doctrine.

I want independent churches in the Grey County area to be able to get ordinary help, including a substitute preacher, without joining a larger denomination. I want the person offering that help to state their qualifications and doctrine, so a church can decide whether that person is acceptable.
I want a church's teaching notes to stay inside that church.
I want to help transcribe public civic materials, and I do not want that work to include church teaching.

I want families who teach their children at home to have teaching materials they can reuse. I want those materials to name the teaching method they use, and I want families whose children attend school to be able to use them too.
I want home-teaching materials that contain no religious claims, so a family that does not share those claims can use them.
I want children in Grey County taught in staffed schools, and I do not want public rooms booked for home-school programs.

groups.title: Goods reused across Grey County boards

statements.text: I want a person in Grey County, Ontario, who will host a small class to be findable, and I want that person's affiliation written down.

groups.title: One more good reused across Grey County boards
notes: Not in the pilot file. One statement, one project, two boards. Not an implication.

statements.text: I want a public notice in Grey County to be readable without needing the recording.

groups.title: Michigan abortion authority, beside the accepted cutoff
notes: These are separate wants. None of them is an implication of the accepted 12-16 week settlement.
Do not give these statements bridge roles.

statements.text: I want Michigan's legislature, rather than a federal statute, to decide whether abortion is legal in Michigan.
I want one federal statute to set the abortion rule for every US state, including Michigan.
I want people in Michigan to keep campaigning for the abortion law they prefer, rather than accepting a cutoff neither side likes.
I want abortion forbidden in Michigan from the start of pregnancy, including during the first 12 weeks.

I want a written comparison of three Michigan proposals — a 12-16 week cutoff, a ban from the start of pregnancy, and no cutoff — that labels each one as a proposal and does not say which rule is in force.
I want a public meeting to publish its question, the statements under discussion, and the notes, without claiming the meeting decided a law.

groups.title: Voting in Grey County
notes: Bridge. Each natural prefers one system and does not say an experiment with another system is welcome. Each modified names that preference and contains the commonality. The commonality says switching off first-past-the-post matters more than which other system, and an experiment with a less-preferred system is welcome. A 2026-10-21 deepseek-v3.2 pass blessed both modifieds and refused the naturals, the first-past-the-post refusal, and the reverse arrow. Those two modified arrows are allowed. keep-first-past-the-post is a refusal on the commonality board.

statements.text: First-past-the-post is an awful voting system. I want more voting in Grey County, Ontario to use some other voting system, preferably ranked choice.
First-past-the-post is an awful voting system. I want more voting in Grey County, Ontario to use some other voting system, preferably approval voting.

First-past-the-post is an awful voting system. I want more voting in Grey County, Ontario to use some other voting system, preferably ranked choice. I have some preferences about which one, but FPTP is particularly awful, so switching away from it is more important to me than which particular other system we use; I'd be happy to see experiments with some other voting system, even if it's not the one I most prefer.

First-past-the-post is an awful voting system. I want more voting in Grey County, Ontario to use some other voting system, preferably approval voting. I have some preferences about which one, but FPTP is particularly awful, so switching away from it is more important to me than which particular other system we use; I'd be happy to see experiments with some other voting system, even if it's not the one I most prefer.

First-past-the-post is an awful voting system. I want more voting in Grey County, Ontario to use some other voting system; I have some preferences about which one, but FPTP is particularly awful, so switching away from it is more important to me than which particular other system we use; I'd be happy to see experiments with some other voting system, even if it's not the one I most prefer.
I want voting in Grey County, Ontario to keep first-past-the-post.

groups.title: Grey County practical-English sessions
notes: Draft bridge from statement-generation-exercises/06-network-society-alliances.json. Modified-to-commonality was blessed on 2026-10-16 and is planned with live-attester evidence. This is not the accepted immigration cluster and it is not accepted seed.

statements.text: I want newcomers in Grey County to be able to learn practical English and how the library, the bus, and a township office work, and I want them to be able to keep their own customs.
If people move to Grey County, they should join the local way of life. I don't want the township running services in origin languages forever.

I want newcomers in Grey County to be able to learn practical English and how the library, the bus, and a township office work, and I want them to be able to keep their own customs. I'd be okay with practical-English sessions in Owen Sound, with childcare, that explain those things, while township business stays in English and the sessions stop short of telling newcomers which customs to keep. I would not want this to become a second township office in origin languages. This isn't my whole view of immigration.

If people move to Grey County, they should be able to function in the local civic life, and I don't want the township running services in origin languages forever. I'd still rather see less immigration, but that is a different question. I'd be okay with practical-English sessions in Owen Sound, with childcare, that explain the library, the bus, and a township office, while township business stays in English and the sessions stop short of telling newcomers which customs to keep. This isn't my whole view of immigration.

groups.title: Owen Sound checkout trial bridge
notes: Draft bridge. Unevaluated. The crypto-merchants planks stay on their own board.

statements.text: I want shops to take crypto so a bank can't decide whether a customer gets to pay.
I'm tired of handing three percent of every sale to the card companies.

I want a willing shop and a willing customer to be able to complete a payment when a bank has blocked that customer. Replacing the banks is a bigger thing than this. I'd be okay with shops in Owen Sound trying a checkout that can take a crypto payment and refund it, show the fee before the customer pays, and keep taking cash and ordinary cards the whole time.

I'm tired of handing three percent of every sale to the card companies. I don't care about crypto as a cause. I'd still be okay with shops in Owen Sound trying a checkout that can take a crypto payment and refund it, show the fee before the customer pays, and keep taking cash and ordinary cards the whole time. If the trial is a bad deal, I want the fees and failures published.
I'd be okay with shops in Owen Sound trying a checkout that can take a crypto payment and refund it, show the fee before the customer pays, and keep taking cash and ordinary cards the whole time.

groups.title: Ordinary opinions and employment
notes: Draft bridge. Good enough for now (2026-10-21). The published-appeal clause is out of the commonality and both modifieds. A 2026-10-21 deepseek-v3.2 pass blessed both shortened modifieds and refused the naturals and the reverse arrow. Those two arrows are allowed. The 2026-10-16 bless is for the longer wording and is not this evidence.

statements.text: Nobody should lose their livelihood because they said something unpopular.
Institutions are ending people's careers over ordinary political opinions, and that should stop.

I don't want someone treated as unemployable for an ordinary political opinion. I still want a workplace to respond to threats, to harassment of coworkers, and to someone refusing to do the job. I'd be okay with it if an ordinary political opinion, by itself, were not grounds for treating someone as unemployable, and if threats, harassment of coworkers, and refusing the work still were. I'd still rather a workplace could tell people not to campaign for a candidate while they are on the clock. I feel less strongly about that than about someone losing a livelihood, and I don't have to defend every opinion.

Institutions should stop ending people's careers over ordinary political opinions. I'd be okay with it if an ordinary political opinion, by itself, were not grounds for treating someone as unemployable, and if threats, harassment of coworkers, and refusing the work still were. I'd still rather a church or a private club could refuse membership over an ordinary political opinion. I feel more strongly about that freedom than about employment rules, and I don't need every sanction anywhere to be forbidden.
I'd be okay with it if an ordinary political opinion, by itself, were not grounds for treating someone as unemployable, and if threats, harassment of coworkers, and refusing the work still were.

groups.title: Ordinary Canada-US ties
notes: Bridge on one want: ordinary purchases and family visits, with the administration question left out. The two modified-to-commonality arrows stay. This is not a second compromise on that same want.

Knowing that other people agree is the signer count on Tally, not a project. The projects are shop-here asks for Grey County businesses that kept ordinary US suppliers and then lost customers over that. The boycott refuses the shared sentence. The narrower sentence only names family visits and does not reject the purchase call. Neither is an implication of the commonality, and neither is published as an arrow. The 2026-10-16 attester refusal is for the longer wording. Not accepted seed.

statements.text: I don't like Trump, and I still think it's foolish for Canadians to cut off ordinary buying and family visits to the US.
Canada should keep its ordinary ties with the US. There's nothing wrong with that.

I don't like the current US administration. I'd still rather Canadians keep buying ordinary goods from US businesses and visiting family there than join a boycott of those ordinary ties. Ordinary Canadians should keep buying from US businesses and visiting family in the US. This is not a statement about the current US administration. I'd still rather people buy the Canadian good when the price and quality are the same. I feel less strongly about that preference than about refusing a boycott.

I want Canadians to keep buying ordinary goods from US businesses and visiting family in the US. Ordinary Canadians should keep buying from US businesses and visiting family in the US. This is not a statement about the current US administration. I'd still rather Canada also keep shared border staffing and ordinary military exercises with the US. I feel more strongly about purchases and family visits than about those, and I am not asking anyone to praise the administration.
Ordinary Canadians should keep buying from US businesses and visiting family in the US. This is not a statement about the current US administration.
I want ordinary Canadians to stop buying from US businesses and to stop family visits to the US while the current administration is in office.
I want Canadians to keep visiting family in the US.

groups.title: Pause new AI capabilities research while work on catastrophic harm continues
notes: Different problems, same limited ask. The shared sentence is the treaty pause. Each milder statement keeps a reason the shared sentence does not contain, so signing the short sentence is not a signature of extinction, of job loss, or of contempt for executives.

Naturals are how someone talks before they have accepted the treaty. Modifieds add that ask. Poles do not contain it. Five modified-to-commonality arrows are allowed after the 2026-10-16 deepseek-v3.2 pass. Naturals, poles, and the reverse arrows stay unpublished.

The shared sentence is: I'd be okay with an international treaty that pauses new research aimed at making AI systems more capable, for the length of that pause, while work continues on how to keep a more capable system from doing catastrophic harm. I'm not saying every current software tool has to be switched off.

statements.text: I'd be okay with an international treaty that pauses new research aimed at making AI systems more capable, for the length of that pause, while work continues on how to keep a more capable system from doing catastrophic harm. I'm not saying every current software tool has to be switched off.
You don't have to be sure that a more capable AI will wipe us out. Even a small chance, something like one percent or ten percent, would be an absurd risk to take in any other context.

I'm not willing to say that a more capable AI is going to wipe us out. I don't need that certainty. Even a small chance of it, something on the order of one or five or ten percent, is an absurd risk to take with everyone's lives. I'd be okay with an international treaty that pauses new research aimed at making AI systems more capable, for the length of that pause, while work continues on how to keep a more capable system from doing catastrophic harm. I'm not saying every current software tool has to be switched off. Signing this is not me joining the people who are already sure.
AI is going to lead to massive job loss. That is not worth it.

What I actually lose sleep over is the jobs. A race to more capable AI looks like a lot of people thrown out of work for a gain I didn't ask for. I'm not claiming I know the chance of extinction. I'd be okay with an international treaty that pauses new research aimed at making AI systems more capable, for the length of that pause, while work continues on how to keep a more capable system from doing catastrophic harm. I'm not saying every current software tool has to be switched off. The pause is the part I came for. The work on catastrophic harm is not my reason.
An increasing number of people inside the AI industry are warning that pushing further has potentially catastrophic consequences.

An increasing number of people who work on these systems are warning that pushing capability further could be catastrophic. I don't build the systems, and I'm not going to pretend I can check their math, but I don't think we should ignore them. I'd be okay with an international treaty that pauses new research aimed at making AI systems more capable, for the length of that pause, while work continues on how to keep a more capable system from doing catastrophic harm. I'm not saying every current software tool has to be switched off. Hearing the warning is not the same as being sure we all die.
I'm not a Luddite, but I'm not blindly in favour of all technology either. This just isn't worth the risk.

I'm not a Luddite, and I'm not against technology in general. Plenty of tools are worth having. A race to more capable AI is a different thing, and I don't think the upside covers the risk. I'd be okay with an international treaty that pauses new research aimed at making AI systems more capable, for the length of that pause, while work continues on how to keep a more capable system from doing catastrophic harm. I'm not saying every current software tool has to be switched off. This isn't a request to smash the machines we already use.
These tech executives are gambling with my children's lives.

I don't trust a handful of tech executives to keep gambling with my children's lives. They can be wrong and still get rich. I'd be okay with an international treaty that pauses new research aimed at making AI systems more capable, for the length of that pause, while work continues on how to keep a more capable system from doing catastrophic harm. I'm not saying every current software tool has to be switched off. My complaint is about who is taking the risk, not a claim that I want every program unplugged.

A superintelligent AI is going to kill us. The work should just stop. A treaty that pauses new capability research while alignment work continues is not enough, because the same labs will keep going the moment the pause slips.
We should not pause AI capabilities research. Falling behind other labs and other countries is the danger I actually take seriously.
